identificationModule.briefTitle: Phase II Trial of Almonertinib Plus Lastet for EGFR+ Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
identificationModule.officialTitle: Phase II Clinical Study of Almonertinib in Combination With Lastet in the First-line Treatment of Locally Advanced or Metastatic Non-small Cell Lung Cancer With EGFR Mutations

collaborators.name: The First Affiliated Hospital of Xiamen University

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to test in Locally Advanced or Metastatic Non-small Cell Lung Cancer patients with EGFR Mutations. The main question it aims to answer is:

Evaluation of the Efficacy and Safety of Aumolertinib in Combination with Lastet for the Treatment of EGFR-Mutated Locally Advanced or Metastatic Non-small Cell Lung Cancer in First-line Therapy.

Participants will be treated with a combination of Aumolertinib and Lastet.

conditions: Lung Cancer Non-small Cell Stage IV

armGroups.label: combination therapy
armGroups.description:
Almonertinib, dosing regimen: 110mg/day orally, once daily in a 28-day cycle, continuously.

Lastet, dosing regimen: 50 mg/day orally, every 28 days in a cycle, two weeks of continuous oral administration, two weeks off.

interventions.name: Almonertinib

primaryOutcomes.description: PFS is defined as the period from the start of treatment until the disease progresses or the patient dies from any cause, whichever came first, assessed up to 24 months

secondaryOutcomes.description: Disease Control Rate (DCR) is to describe the proportion of patients who have achieved a response to treatment that includes not only complete and partial responses but also stable disease.
The Duration of Response (DoR) is a clinical measure to determine the length of time that a tumor continues to respond to treatment without the cancer worsening.
The Objective Response Rate (ORR) is a key metric used in oncology to assess the proportion of patients in a study or treatment group who achieve an objective response (CR or PR).
OS is measured from the date of the initiation of treatment to the date of death from any cause, whichever came first, assessed up to 24 months
